newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek fx forwards dip, depos hold, T-bills snapped.
newsitem.headline: Greek fx forwards dip, depos hold, T-bills snapped.

text.p: Greek depos were holding morning levels but forex forwards had dipped in short periods up to a month in late dealings and sales of T-bills appeared to be exceptionally strong, traders said.

"Depos are stable but short-term forex forwards in periods up to a month have retreated as some major banks loaded with drachmas seek a better return than the central bank's 12.40 percent overnight bid," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
The central bank intervened on both sides of the overnight, draining liquidity at 12.40 percent and injecting cash at 13.40 percent.
Dealers said preliminary evidence showed that T-bills sold well today.
"It look as if sales of T-bills went very well exceeding 500 billion drachmas," said a dealer at a state bank.
A number of dealers said they expected strong retail demand for this T-bill issue because of talk about an upcoming withholding tax on state securities.

The finance ministry issued three-, six- and 12-month T-bills on October 31 at 12.30 percent, 11.70 percent and 11.50 percent respectively, down from 12.70 percent, 12.10 percent and 11.90 percent at end-September.
The mark was quoted at 157.10/20 drachmas from Thursday's 157.085 fix, the dollar at 237.93/98 drachmas from 237.560 and the Ecu at 301.52/62 from 301.480 drachmas.

"Ecu/drachma landed higher at the fixing," said a forex dealer. "It looks as if ecu is heading higher, to get closer to the central bank's pre-announced target by year-end and some players might decide to take profits."
